paragraphs: All references to "we," "us," "our," "Rocky Brands," or the "Company" in this Annual Report on Form 10-K mean Rocky Brands, Inc. and our subsidiaries.

We are a leading designer, manufacturer and marketer of premium quality footwear and apparel marketed under a portfolio of well recognized brand names, including The Original Muck Boot Company ("Muck"), XTRATUF, Rocky, Durango, Georgia Boot, Lehigh CustomFit ("Lehigh"), Ranger, and the licensed brand Michelin. Our brands have a long history of representing high quality, comfortable, functional, and durable footwear and our products are organized around six target markets: work, outdoor, western, commercial military, duty, and military. Our footwear products incorporate varying features and are positioned across a range of suggested retail price points from $45.00 for our value priced products to $680.00 for our premium products. In addition, as part of our strategy of outfitting consumers from head-to-toe, we market complementary branded apparel and accessories that we believe leverage the strength and positioning of each of our brands.
The Company's portfolio of brands is organized into the following reportable segments, in which our products are distributed:
Wholesale Retail Contract Manufacturing Wholesale

We distribute Muck, XTRATUF, Rocky, Durango, Georgia Boot, Lehigh, Ranger, and Michelin products through a wide range of Wholesale distribution channels throughout the world. Our Wholesale channels vary by product line and include sporting goods stores, outdoor retailers, independent shoe retailers, hardware stores, mass merchants, uniform stores, farm store chains, specialty safety stores, specialty retailers, and online retailers. As of
December 31, 2025 , our products were offered for sale in thousands of
retail locations across the U.S. and Canada as well as several international markets, such as Europe.

We sell to wholesale accounts in the U.S. through a dedicated in-house sales team, and exclusive, as well as independent, sales representatives who carry our branded products and other non-competing products. Our sales force is organized around major accounts, including Amazon, Boot Barn, Tractor Supply Company, and Bass Pro, and around our target markets: work, outdoor, western, commercial military, duty, and military. Our sales force is also organized around brands, regions and customers to target a broad range of distribution channels. All our salespeople actively call on their retail customer base to educate them on the quality, comfort, technical features, and breadth of our product lines and to ensure that our products are displayed effectively at retail locations.
Our Wholesale distribution channels vary by market:
Our work-related products are sold primarily through work-related retailers, farm and ranch stores, specialty safety stores, independent shoe stores, hardware stores, and online retailers;
Our outdoor products are sold primarily through sporting goods stores, outdoor specialty stores, online retailers, and mass merchants;
Our western products are sold through western stores, work stores, specialty farm and ranch stores, online retailers, and fashion-oriented footwear retailers;
Our commercial military products are sold primarily through base exchanges, such as the Army Air Force Exchange Store (AAFES) and consumer e-commerce websites; and
Our duty products are sold primarily through uniform stores, and online retailers. Retail

headings: Business Risks
A majority of our products are produced outside the continental U.S. where we are subject to the risks of international commerce and other international conditions.
Our success depends on our ability to anticipate consumer trends.
We depend on a limited number of suppliers for key production materials, and disruptions in the supply of such materials could interrupt product manufacturing and increase product costs.
The emergence or persistence of geopolitical instability may disrupt the global economy, the impacts of which may negatively impact our business, financial, condition and results of operations.
Our outdoor and insulated products are seasonal and sales of such products are sensitive to weather conditions.
Our business could suffer if our third-party manufacturers violate labor, environmental or other applicable laws or fail to conform to generally accepted ethical standards.
The growth of our business will be dependent upon the availability of adequate capital.
Our current level of indebtedness could adversely affect our business by increasing our borrowing costs and decreasing our overall business flexibility.
We must comply with the restrictive covenants contained in our credit facilities.
Interest rate increases could adversely affect our financial results.

Our financial success is influenced by the success of our wholesale customers, and the loss of such a key customer could have a material adverse effect on our financial condition and results of operations.
Certain of our larger wholesale customers may develop and manufacture competing products under their own brands and reduce purchases of our branded products.
We currently manufacture a portion of our products, and we may not be able to do so in the future at costs that are competitive with those of competitors who source their goods.
If our efforts to establish and protect our trademarks, patents and other intellectual property are unsuccessful, the value of our brands could suffer.
An impairment of intangibles, including goodwill, could have an adverse impact to the Company's results of operations.
Our success depends on our ability to forecast sales.
Our dividend policy may change.
Industry Risks
The continued shift in the third-party marketplace from traditional independent retailers to large mass merchandisers may result in decreased margins.
The shift in consumer shopping to online retailers and our increased online sales pose various risks which may negatively impact our business.
General Risk Factors
Changes to U.S. tax, tariff and import/export regulations may have a negative effect on global economic conditions, financial markets and our business.

We are implementing a new enterprise resource planning system, and challenges with the implementation of the system may have an adverse effect on our business, financial condition results of operations
There are risks, including stock market volatility, inherent in owning our common stock.
Disruption of our information technology systems and e-commerce platforms could adversely affect our business
A cybersecurity breach could have a material adverse effect on our business and reputation.
We are subject to certain environmental and other regulations.
We are subject to periodic litigation and other regulatory proceedings, which could result in the unexpected expenditure of time and resources.
Loss of services of our key personnel could adversely affect our business.

We may use artificial intelligence in our business, which could result in reputational harm, competitive harm, and legal liability, and adversely affect our business, results of operations and financial condition.
paragraphs: An investment in our common stock is subject to certain risks inherent in our business. Before making an investment decision, investors should carefully consider the risks and uncertainties described below, together with all of the other information included or incorporated by reference in this Annual Report on Form 10-K. If any of the following risks occur, our business, results of operations, financial condition, and cash flows could be materially and adversely affected. These described risks are not the only risks facing us. Additional risks and uncertainties not known to us or that we deem to be immaterial also may materially adversely affect our business, results of operations, financial condition, and cash flows. If any of these risks were to materialize, the value of our common stock could decline significantly.

Expanding our brands into new footwear and apparel markets may be difficult and expensive, and if we are unable to successfully continue such expansion, our brands may be adversely affected, and we may not achieve our planned sales growth.

Our growth strategy is founded substantially on the expansion of our brands into new footwear and apparel markets. New products that we introduce may not be successful with consumers or one or more of our brands may fall out of favor with consumers. If we are unable to anticipate, identify or react appropriately to changes in consumer preferences, we may not grow as fast as we plan to grow. This could cause our sales to decline, brand image to suffer and operating performance to deteriorate.

Furthermore, achieving market acceptance for new products will likely require us to exert substantial product development and marketing efforts, which could result in a material increase in our expenses, and there can be no assurance that we will have the resources necessary to undertake such efforts. Material increases in our expenses could adversely impact our results of operations and cash flows.

We may also encounter difficulties in producing new products that we did not anticipate during the development stage. Our development schedules for new products are difficult to predict and are subject to change as a result of shifting priorities in response to consumer preferences and competing products. If we are not able to efficiently manufacture newly-developed products in quantities sufficient to support retail distribution, we may not be able to recoup our investment in the development of new products. Failure to gain market acceptance for new products that we introduce could impede our growth, reduce our profits, adversely affect the image of our brands, erode our competitive position and result in long term harm to our business.

paragraphs: This Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations ("MD&A") describes the matters that we consider to be important to understanding the results of our operations for each of the two years in the period ended December 31, 2025 and 2024, and our capital resources and liquidity as of December 31, 2025 and 2024. For the discussion of the changes in our results of operations and statement of cash flows between the years ended December 31, 2024 and December 31, 2023, refer to Item 7, "Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations", of our Annual Report on Form 10-K for the year ended December 31, 2024, filed with the SEC on March 17, 2025, which is available on the SEC's website at https://www.sec.gov/edgar/search/ and our corporate website at www.rockybrands.com. We analyze the results of our operations for the last two years (including trends in the overall business), followed by a discussion of our cash flows and liquidity, our credit facilities, and our contractual commitments. We then provide a review of the critical accounting policies and estimates we have made that we believe are most important to the understanding of our MD&A and our Consolidated Financial Statements. We conclude our MD&A with information on recent accounting pronouncements we adopted during the year, as well as those not yet adopted that are expected to have an impact on our financial accounting practices.

The following discussion should be read in conjunction with our Consolidated Financial Statements and the notes thereto, included elsewhere herein. The forward-looking statements in this section and other parts of this Annual Report on Form 10-K involve risks and uncertainties including statements regarding our plans, objectives, goals, strategies and financial performance. Our actual results could differ materially from the results anticipated in these forward-looking statements as a result of factors set forth under the caption "Safe Harbor Statement under the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995" below. The Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995 provides a "safe harbor" for forward-looking statements made by or on behalf of the Company.

We are a leading designer, manufacturer and marketer of premium quality footwear and apparel marketed under a portfolio of well recognized brand names including Muck, XTRATUF, Rocky, Durango, Georgia Boot, Lehigh, Ranger, and the licensed brand Michelin. Our portfolio of brands is organized into three reportable segments in which our product is distributed: Wholesale, Retail, and Contract Manufacturing. The reportable segments are targeted around six distinct product lines: work, outdoor, western, duty, commercial military, and military. We frequently experience significant seasonal fluctuations in our business as many of our footwear products and product lines are used by consumers in adverse weather conditions. Accordingly, average inventory levels have been highest during the second and third quarters of each year and sales have been highest in the last two quarters of the year. Our footwear products incorporate varying features and are positioned across a range of suggested retail price points from $45.00 for our value priced products to $680.00 for our premium products. As a part of our strategy of outfitting consumers from head-to-toe, we market complementary branded apparel and accessories that we believe leverage the strength and positioning of each of our brands.

In our Wholesale business, we distribute our products through a wide range of distribution channels representing thousands of retail store locations in the U.S., the U.K. and other international markets such as Europe. Our Wholesale channels vary by product line and include sporting goods stores, outdoor retailers, independent shoe retailers, hardware stores, mass merchants, uniform stores, farm store chains, specialty safety stores, specialty retailers, and online retailers. Our Retail business includes direct sales of our products to consumers through our business-to-business web platform, e-commerce websites, third-party marketplaces and our Rocky Outdoor Gear Store. Our Contract Manufacturing segment includes sales to the U.S. Military, private label sales and any sales to customers in which we are contracted to manufacture or source a specific footwear product for a customer.

Over the last two years, we have seen a shift in our total mix of sales, as the growth of our Retail segment continues to outpace the growth in our Wholesale and Contract Manufacturing segments. Growth in our Retail segment was primarily driven by increased sales on our owned e-commerce websites and third-party marketplaces, as we placed an emphasis on our direct-to-consumer business, partially through increased digital marketing in response to an ongoing shift among consumers to online retailers.

During the second quarter of 2024, we amended and restated our Original ABL Facility (as such term is defined in Note 7 - Long-Term Debt of our Consolidated Financial Statements) which resulted in a restated $175.0 million revolving credit facility and a new $50.0 million term facility. The proceeds from this transaction were used to retire our existing senior secured term loan facility with TCW Asset Management Company, LLC as of April 26, 2024. This transaction resulted in an expense of $2.6 million, consisting of a loss on extinguishment of term debt in the amount of $1.1 million and a $1.5 million prepayment penalty, which are included in Interest Expense and Other -net within the Consolidated Statements of Operations for the twelve months ended December 31, 2024. See Note 7 - Long-Term Debt of our Consolidated Financial Statements for further information regarding our long-term debt.

In the first quarter of 2025, we announced a share repurchase program, which was approved by the Board of Directors to allow the Company to repurchase up to $7.5 million of the Company's outstanding common stock. During the first quarter of 2025, the Company repurchased 10,456 shares of common stock under the plan using cash flows generated from operations.

The year ended December 31, 2025 was a year of growth, led by top-line expansion in our Retail segment, particularly in our direct-to-consumer selling channel. We delivered higher margins in 2025 compared to 2024 in both our Wholesale and Retail segments. While the additional tariffs imposed in the second quarter of 2025 created margin pressures in the latter half of the year, we were able to ease the burden by diversifying our sourcing and leveraging our manufacturing facilities in the Dominican Republic and Puerto Rico as well as benefit from implementing price increases prior to realizing the impact of the tariffs. While operating expenses were up slightly to the year ago period, we were able to significantly increase our bottom line as a result of interest expense and tax savings.

Our growth strategy is founded substantially on the expansion of our brands into new footwear and apparel markets. New products that we introduce may not be successful with consumers or one or more of our brands may fall out of favor with consumers. If we are unable to anticipate, identify or react appropriately to changes in consumer preferences, we may not grow as fast as we plan to grow, or our sales may decline, and our brand image and operating performance may suffer.

Furthermore, achieving market acceptance for new products will likely require us to exert substantial product development and marketing efforts, which could result in a material increase in expenses to which there can be no assurance that we will have the resources necessary to undertake such efforts. Material increases in expenses could adversely impact our results of operations and cash flows.

We may also encounter difficulties in producing new products that we did not anticipate during the development stage. Our development schedules for new products are difficult to predict and are subject to change as a result of shifting priorities in response to consumer preferences and competing products. If we are not able to efficiently manufacture newly developed products in quantities sufficient to support retail distribution, we may not be able to recoup our investment in the development of new products. Failure to gain market acceptance for new products that we introduce could impede our growth, reduce our profits, adversely affect the image of our brands, erode our competitive position, and result in long term harm to our business.

Our business is subject to a highly evolving and everchanging macroeconomic environment, including changes in tariffs, taxes, and industry changes. We continue to monitor changes in policy impacting global trade, including tariffs, which have been dynamic, unpredictable, and subject to ongoing modification. Beginning in early 2025, pursuant to the International Emergency Economic Powers Act ("IEEPA"), the U.S. presidential administration modified and imposed significant additional tariffs on products imported from various countries, including those countries where we primarily source our products. During the year ended December 31, 2025, we paid approximately $18.7 million in IEEPA tariffs. More recently, in February 2026, the U.S. Supreme Court ruled that certain tariffs imposed under the IEEPA were unlawful. Following the Supreme Court's decision, the U.S. presidential administration announced its intention to invoke other laws to collect tariffs and announced new tariffs on imports from all countries, in addition to any existing non-IEEPA tariffs. There remains substantial uncertainty regarding the duration of existing and newly announced tariffs, potential changes or pauses to such tariffs, tariff levels, and whether additional tariffs or other retaliatory actions may be imposed, modified, or suspended. During 2025, we have implemented, and plan to continue to implement, as needed, various mitigation strategies including adjusting the prices of our products, adjusting the countries from which we source our products and further leveraging our own manufacturing facilities in the Dominican Republic and Puerto Rico. Proposed or enacted tariffs and changes to U.S. trading policies may be restituted, paused, removed, or changed at any time and to the extent we are unable to successfully mitigate any negative impacts it could adversely affect our business, financial condition and results of operation.

paragraphs: 本公司管理層對財務狀況與營運結果之分析（"MD&A"）說明我們認為對瞭解我們在2025年12月31日及2024年12月31日兩年期間營運結果重要的事項，以及我們在2025年12月31日及2024年12月31日的資本資源與流動性。有關我們營運結果與現金流量變動之討論，請參閱我們2024年12月31日年度報告表10-K中第7項"管理層對財務狀況與營運結果之分析"，該報告於2025年3月17日提交至證券交易委員會（SEC），並可在SEC網站https://www.sec.gov/edgar/search/及本公司網站www.rockybrands.com取得。我們分析過去兩年營運結果（包括整體業務趨勢），隨後討論現金流量與流動性、信用融資及契約義務。我們再提供對我們認為最重要的會計政策與會計估計之審閱。我們以最近採用的會計準則及預期將影響我們財務會計作法之未採用準則結尾。
請配合本公司合併財務報表及其附註說明閱讀本段內容。本節及其他部分的年度報告表10-K中之預測性陳述涉及風險與不確定性，包括有關我們計畫、目標、策略與財務表現之陳述。我們實際結果可能與預測性陳述中預期結果有重大差異，原因請參閱下述"1995年私人證券訴訟改革法案之安全港聲明"。1995年私人證券訴訟改革法案為本公司或代表本公司所作預測性陳述提供"安全港"保護。

本公司為領先的高品質鞋類與服飾設計、製造與行銷公司，產品行銷於包括Muck、XTRATUF、Rocky、Durango、Georgia Boot、Lehigh、Ranger及授權品牌Michelin等知名品牌組合。我們的品牌組合分為三個應報告分部，產品透過這些分部銷售： Wholesale（批發）、Retail（零售）及Contract Manufacturing（委製）。應報告分部針對六種不同的產品線：工作、戶外、西部、勤務、商業軍事及軍事。我們經常經驗到顯著的季節性波動，因許多鞋類產品與產品線被消費者在惡劣天氣條件下使用。因此，平均存貨水準在每年第二及第三季為最高，銷售額則在每年最後兩季為最高。我們的鞋類產品包含多樣特徵，並根據建議零售價格點從45.00美元的價值型產品至680.00美元的高階產品進行定位。作為我們從頭到腳為消費者提供裝備的策略一部分，我們行銷補充品牌的服飾與配件，我們認為這些產品能發揮各品牌強度與定位。

在 Wholesale（批發）業務中，我們透過廣泛的分銷渠道銷售產品，這些渠道代表美國、英國及其他國際市場如歐洲的數千家零售商店。我們的 Wholesale（批發）渠道因產品線而異，包括運動用品商店、戶外零售商、獨立鞋類零售商、五金店、大型零售商、制服商店、農場連鎖商店、專業安全商店、專業零售商及線上零售商。我們的 Retail（零售）業務包括透過我們的企業對企業（B2B）網站平台、電商網站、第三方市場平台及 Rocky Outdoor Gear Store（Rocky 戶外裝備商店）直接向消費者銷售產品。我們的 Contract Manufacturing（委製）分部包括銷售給美國軍隊、私人標籤銷售及任何我們被委託製造或來源特定鞋類產品給客戶的銷售。
在過去兩年，我們觀察到總銷售組成的變化，因 Retail（零售）分部的成長速度持續快於 Wholesale（批發）及 Contract Manufacturing（委製）分部。Retail（零售）分部的成長主要由我們自有電商網站及第三方市場平台的銷售增加所驅動，因我們加強了對直接對消費者業務的重視，部分透過增加數位行銷以回應消費者持續轉向線上零售商的趨勢。

在2024年第二季，我們修改並重述了我們的Original ABL Facility（如在我們合併財務報表的第7項長期債務附註中所定義），結果產生重述後的175.0百萬美元循環信貸融資及新的50.0百萬美元定期融資。此交易所得資金用於償還我們於2024年4月26日與TCW Asset Management Company, LLC簽訂的現有高階抵押定期貸款融資。此交易產生2.6百萬美元費用，包含1.1百萬美元的定期貸款債務終止損失及1.5百萬美元的預付款罰款，這些費用包含在2024年12月31日財年合併營運損益表的利息費用及其他-淨項目中。有關我們長期債務的進一步資訊，請參閱我們合併財務報表的第7項長期債務附註。
在2025年第一季，我們宣佈了一項股票回購計畫，該計畫經董事會批准，允許本公司回購最多7.5百萬美元的本公司流通普通股。在2025年第一季，本公司根據計畫使用營運產生的現金回購了10,456股普通股。

2025年12月31日財年為成長年，由零售分部的營收擴張帶動，特別是在我們的直接對消費者銷售通路。我們在2025年的毛利率較2024年在 Wholesale（批發）及 Retail（零售）分部均有提高。雖然2025年第二季額外加徵的關稅在該年後半段造成毛利率壓力，但我們透過多元化來源及利用多明尼加共和國及波多黎各的製造設施，以及在關稅影響前實施價格上漲，成功緩解了壓力。雖然營運費用較去年同期略增，但我們因利息費用及稅務節省而大幅提高淨利潤。
本公司成長策略主要建立在將品牌拓展至新鞋類與服飾市場。我們所推出的新產品可能無法獲得消費者青睞，或其中一個或多個品牌可能不再受消費者歡迎。若本公司無法預見、識別或適時回應消費者偏好的變動，本公司可能無法如預期般成長，或銷售額可能下降，且本公司品牌形象與營運表現可能受損。
此外，要讓新產品獲得市場接受度，本公司可能需要投入大量產品開發與行銷努力，這可能會導致費用大幅增加，而本公司無法保證是否有足夠資源進行這些努力。費用大幅增加可能會對本公司營運成果與現金流產生不利影響。
本公司也可能在生產預期之外的新產品時遇到困難。新產品的開發時程難以預測，且可能因應消費者偏好與競爭產品而改變優先順序。若本公司無法高效地以足夠數量生產新開發的產品，以支持零售分銷，本公司可能無法彌補在新產品開發上的投資。未能獲得新產品的市場接受度，可能會阻礙本公司成長，降低利潤，對品牌形象產生不利影響，削弱競爭優勢，並對本公司業務造成長期損害。

本公司業務面臨高度變動且持續演進的總體經濟環境，包括關稅、稅收與產業變動。本公司持續監測影響全球貿易的政策變動，包括關稅，這些關稅已呈現動態、不可預測且持續修改的特質。自2025年初起，根據國際緊急經濟權力法（"IEEPA"），美國總統行政部門修改並施加了對來自多個國家進口產品的顯著額外關稅，包括本公司主要進口產品的國家。在2025年12月31日為結業年度，本公司支付了約18.7百萬美元的IEEPA關稅。最近，在2026年2月，美國最高法院裁定某些根據IEEPA施加的關稅違法。在最高法院作出裁決後，美國總統行政部門宣佈有意透過其他法律來徵收關稅，並宣佈對所有國家進口商品的新關稅，包括任何現有的非IEEPA關稅。現有及新宣佈關稅的持續時間、潛在變動或暫停、關稅水準，以及是否會施加、修改或暫停其他關稅或報復性措施，仍存在相當大的不確定性。在2025年，本公司已實施並計畫根據需要持續實施各種緩衝策略，包括調整產品價格、調整進口國家，以及進一步利用本公司在多明尼加共和國與波多黎各的自有製造設施。所提出的或已通過的關稅與美國貿易政策變動，可能隨時被撤回、暫停、刪除或修改，而本公司若無法成功緩衝任何負面影響，可能會對本公司業務、財務狀況與營運成果產生不利影響。
2025年財務概覽 淨銷售額較2024年成長6.2%，達482.0百萬美元；
毛利率較2024年的39.4%淨銷售額百分比成長150個基點，達2025年40.9%淨銷售額百分比；

headings: Business Risks
我們大多數產品是在美國本土以外的地區生產，因此我們面臨國際貿易及其他國際環境的風險。
我們的成功取決於我們預測消費者趨勢的能力。
我們依賴有限數量的供應商提供關鍵生產材料，若這些材料的供應中斷，可能會影響產品製造並提高產品成本。
地緣政治不穩定的出現或持續存在，可能會干擾全球經濟，其影響可能對我們的業務、財務狀況及營運成果產生負面影響。
我們的戶外及保溫產品具有季節性，這些產品的銷售會受到天氣條件的影響。
若我們的第三方製造商違反勞動、環境或其他適用法律，或未能符合普遍接受的倫理標準，可能會對我們的業務造成影響。
我們業務的成長將取決於取得充足資金的可行性。
本公司目前的負債水平可能不利於業務，透過提高借款成本及降低整體業務靈活性。
本公司必須遵守信用融資協議中所包含的限制性契約條款。
利率上升可能不利於財務結果。
本公司財務表現受 wholesale 客戶表現影響，若失去關鍵客戶，可能對財務狀況及營運結果產生重大不利影響。
部分較大型的 wholesale 客戶可能自行開發製造競爭產品並以自有品牌銷售，進而減少本公司品牌產品的採購。
本公司目前製造部分產品，未來可能無法以與競爭對手更具競爭力的成本製造產品。
若本公司建立及保護商標、專利及其他智慧財產權的措施未能成功，將可能影響品牌價值。
商譽及其他無形資產減損，可能對本公司營運結果產生不利影響。
本公司之成功取決於本公司預測銷售能力。
本公司股息政策可能變更。
產業風險
第三方市場持續從傳統獨立零售商轉向大型通路商，可能導致毛利率下降。
消費者購物轉向線上零售商，以及本公司線上銷售增加，可能產生各種風險，可能對本公司業務產生負面影響。
一般風險因素
美國稅收、關稅及進出口規範之變更，可能對全球經濟情況、財務市場及本公司業務產生負面影響。
本公司正在實施新的企業資源規劃系統，系統實施過程中的挑戰可能對本公司業務、財務狀況及營運成果產生負面影響
本公司普通股之持有面臨風險，包括股市波動性。
資訊科技系統與電子商務平台之中斷可能對本公司業務造成不利影響。
網路安全事件可能對本公司業務與聲譽造成重大不利影響。
本公司受某些環境及其他法規之約束。
本公司可能涉及定期訴訟及其他法規程序，此等程序可能導致意外耗用時間與資源。
本公司關鍵人員之服務喪失可能對業務造成不利影響。
本公司可能於業務中使用人工智慧，此可能導致聲譽損害、競爭損害及法律責任，並對業務、營運成果與財務狀況造成不利影響。
paragraphs: 投資本公司普通股有其固有的風險。在做出投資決定前，投資人應仔細考慮下列所描述的風險與不確定性，並配合本年度報告表10-K所包含或參考的其他資訊。若任何下列風險發生，將可能對本公司業務、營運結果、財務狀況與現金流造成重大且不利的影響。上述所描述的風險並非本公司所面臨的唯一風險。尚有其他風險與不確定性，可能未為本公司所知或認為不重要，但同樣可能對本公司業務、營運結果、財務狀況與現金流造成重大且不利的影響。若任何上述風險實現，本公司普通股的價值可能大幅下跌。
將我們的品牌拓展至新的鞋類與服飾市場可能困難且成本高昂，若我們無法成功持續進行此種拓展，將可能對我們的品牌造成不利影響，且我們可能無法達成預期的銷售成長。
我們的成長策略主要建立在將品牌拓展至新的鞋類與服飾市場。我們所推出的產品可能無法受到消費者歡迎，或我們的某個或某幾個品牌可能不再受到消費者青睞。若我們無法預測、識別或適當地回應消費者偏好的變化，我們可能無法如預期般成長。這可能會導致我們的銷售額下降、品牌形象受損，以及營運表現惡化。
此外，要讓新產品獲得市場接受度，將需要我們投入大量產品開發與行銷努力，這可能會導致我們的費用大幅增加，且無法保證我們擁有足夠的資源來進行這些努力。費用的大幅增加可能對我們的營運結果與現金流造成不利影響。
我們也可能在生產預期之外的新產品時遇到困難。我們新產品的開發時程難以預測，且會因應消費者偏好與競爭產品的變化而調整優先順序。若我們無法高效地製造新開發的產品，以足夠數量支援零售分銷，我們可能無法彌補在新產品開發上的投資。新產品若無法獲得市場接受度，將可能阻礙我們的成長，減少我們的利潤，對品牌形象造成不利影響，削弱我們的競爭地位，並對我們的業務造成長期傷害。
我們的大多數產品是在越南、中國、多明尼加共和國、柬埔寨、波多黎各、印度與墨西哥製造。因此，我們的業務面臨某些海外營運的風險，包括：
